title: Agent Control Decisions on the Request Trace
dataSources: Control spans (`add_control_span`, shown with a shield in the console) on the request traces
description: Records every Agent Control decision on the request's trace as a control span, so reviewers can see which control fired, on which step, and what the agent did next.
value: Control decisions without context cannot be audited. On the trace, each deny, steer or observe sits next to the request and the response, which is the evidence auditors ask for.
implementation: Run each decorated step inside an open trace so the control span lands on it. Where the app records a control result itself, use `add_control_span`.
visualization: Trace view with control spans marked by a shield.

references.title: Splunk Agent Observability: Agent Control overview

knownFalsePositives: Steps run outside a trace (for example background jobs) produce no control span; trace them or record their decisions separately.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites

A Splunk Agent Observability project for the application and one Agent Stream per environment or agent inside it. Do not create a second project for the same application: a second project splits the traces. The agent reads `SPLUNK_AO_PROJECT` and `SPLUNK_AO_AGENT_STREAM` from the environment. SaaS tenants authenticate with `SPLUNK_AO_REALM` and `SPLUNK_AO_O11Y_TOKEN`; on-prem tenants with `SPLUNK_AO_API_KEY` plus `SPLUNK_AO_CONSOLE_URL`. Install the SDK with `pip install splunk-ao` (`pip install "splunk-ao[langchain]"` for the LangChain callback). Agent Control is a separate server and a separate install (`agent-control-sdk`, plus `agent-control-evaluators`; one of those packages is still named `agent-control-evaluator-galileo`, the platform's old name).

Step 1 — Instrument the agent

The app calls `agent_control.init` and decorates the step with `@control(step_name=...)`. There are two ways to bind a control, and a tenant uses one of them. The Splunk Agent Observability docs pass the resolved `agent_stream_id` (not the stream name) as `target_id` and attach the control to the stream in the console. The SDK path calls `init(agent_name=...)`, creates a policy, adds the control to it, and assigns the policy to that agent name. If the repo already has an example, follow it. Run the decorated step inside an open trace so the control span lands on that trace.

Step 2 — Configure in Splunk Agent Observability

Open a trace that hit a control. The console marks control spans with a shield.

Step 3 — Validate

Trigger a control on a test stream and confirm the control span sits on that request's trace. This use case was written from the Splunk Agent Observability documentation without access to a tenant, so it ships as a draft. Confirm each step in the Splunk Agent Observability console before promoting it.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Use the traces with control spans as evidence in control reviews.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

Control span missing: the decorated step ran before `start_trace` or after the trace was concluded.
grandmaExplanation: Every time a guard steps in, it is written into the same record as the question and the answer.

productArtifacts.title: Run controlled steps inside an open trace
productArtifacts.body:
logger.start_trace(input=user_text, name="request", metadata={"consumer": user_id})
logger.add_agent_span(input=user_text, name="answer", metadata={"consumer": user_id})
result = ""
try:
    result = run_sql(query)  # decorated with @control(step_name="run_sql")
finally:
    logger.conclude(output=str(result), conclude_all=True)
